verdict.summary: cartservice became slow because its backing Redis (redis-cart) started responding slowly, so cart reads/writes blocked and the latency propagated up through frontend and checkoutservice to the loadgenerator.
verdict.reasoning: cartservice alerted 15s before everything else, and every other alerting service is one of its callers (frontend -> cartservice, checkoutservice -> cartservice, frontend -> checkoutservice, loadgenerator drives frontend). The blast radius is exactly the caller closure plus checkout's fan-out peers, which is what pure propagation looks like rather than independent failures. cartservice has no downstream in the catalog, so whatever slowed it is off-graph; the only off-graph thing it owns is redis-cart, which is called synchronously on every add-to-cart and every cart read. Slow Redis (eviction pressure, AOF rewrite, a big keyspace scan, or a failover) is the standard way this service stalls while staying up and merely 'high latency' rather than erroring. Remediation is most likely restarting/replacing the Redis instance (and cartservice to clear its pool).
